newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Nat Mortgage Bank 96 pretax up 80pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Nat Mortgage Bank 96 pretax up 80pct.

text.p: Greece's state National Mortgage Bank posted pretax profits of 36.08 billion drachmas for fiscal 1996 against 20.06 billion in 1995, an increase of 80 percent, its president Vassilis Rapanos told shareholders on Wednesday.

"The bank made a leap in its profitability in 1996," said Rapanos. "Pretax profits would have been 41.4 billion drachmas in 1996, more than double its 1995 profits, if the bank had followed the same policy on provisions as in the previous years."
Rapanos was speaking to the annual general shareholders' meeting.
The shareholders approved the board's proposal to raise provisions to 28.1 billion drachmas in 1996 from 20.8 billion in 1995.
The bank, a subsidiary of the state National Bank of Greece, increased its mortgage lending by 74.5 percent to 136.8 billion drachmas in 1996 from 78.4 billion in 1995, he added.

The merger of the National Mortgage Bank with the National Housing Bank would be the main event in 1997, said Rapanos, pointing out that the merger would strengthen his bank's position in mortgage credit.
National Mortgage Bank's equity capital stood at 76.6 billion drachmas at the end of 1996 from 58.3 billion at the end of 1995.
The bank will pay a dividend per share of 900 drachmas for fiscal 1996 compared to 450 drachmas in 1995.
